minutes.headline: Finance Committee questioned the treasurer on low investment yields and gave input on the FY25 capital plan ranking.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the town's year-end cash report and municipal investments with the treasurer. Members pressed for higher returns, and she explained the legal limits on how municipal funds may be invested. They then discussed capital planning input for FY25, including school project shifts, MSBA uncertainty, and whether Parks should be prioritized separately from facilities. The budget season calendar and future meetings were reviewed, and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Advocated for Parks capital requests (survey and conceptual design, Marshall Pond weed removal, Wallace basketball court resurfacing); said Parks sits under facilities and has had five leaderships in three years; and that Parks funding has been neglected, with the revolving fund paying for the beach house repair.
Thanked the committee for allowing her to take part in the discussions.

budget_items.topic: Liquid investment accounts at multiple banks
budget_items.what_was_said: Member noted three investment accounts with widely differing interest rates; the treasurer said a new account was opened with a promotional rate.
Member argued money markets could return around 5% and asked why long-term funds earn less; the treasurer said funds must follow the legal list and safety rules.
The treasurer said some banks charge no fees and give lower interest, and the lock box service is free because of the investment agreement.
Member said MMDT rates far exceed the current holdings and that a percentage point on a large balance is a lot per year.

budget_items.topic: Septic grant and small restricted accounts
budget_items.what_was_said: An old septic loan grant account has sat for years earning little and is now being spent on the parks; grant restrictions prevent consolidation.
A member flagged FY26 items that might be funded through Green Communities grants.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill window study and replacement
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion about a window study moving between fiscal years in the school capital submission.
A member asked about having separate lists for small and large capital projects given the threshold.
Members questioned the balance of the parks revolving fund, and a commission member said postings were incomplete and the true balance is lower.
The remaining expense budget would fund a few attendees at the MMA meeting; the budget was previously doubled.

decisions.decision: Members will individually rank capital projects over the next week and send input to the chair, with consolidated ranking meetings on the 18th and 20th/21st.
No meeting until January 11th; the reorganization and committee liaison assignments are planned for that meeting.
An appointment committee meeting is planned for the 13th to try to seat a seventh member.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes; members gave individual input on ranking FY25 capital projects, with consolidated ranking meetings set for the 18th and the 20th or 21st.
Members pressed the treasurer on why stabilization and OPEB funds earn less than money markets; she said funds must follow the legal investment list and safety rules.
A member said state pool (MMDT) rates far exceed current bank holdings, and that a percentage point on a large balance is a lot per year.
Members questioned the Parks revolving fund balance; a commission member said postings were incomplete and the true balance is lower.
No meeting is planned until January 11th, when the reorganization and liaison assignments are expected; an appointment committee meets on the 13th to try to seat a seventh member.

why_it_matters: The interest the town earns on its cash and reserve funds offsets what must be raised from taxpayers, and the committee is testing whether the legal limits on municipal investing leave that return low.
The capital ranking shapes which FY25 projects, including school and Parks items, reach a Town Meeting vote, and it is still unsettled whether Parks should be ranked separately from facilities.
